title: What one 8-hour night costs
sub: Full-power ceilings; thermostats and auto-off make real use lower
footer: Cost = watts ÷ 1,000 × 8 hours × price. Prices: EIA US residential average 18.16¢/kWh (Aug 2026). Our arithmetic.

name: howto
title: Find your own cost per night in five minutes
sub: The same formula works for any heater, pad or blanket
footer: Formula from the U.S. Department of Energy's 'What does it cost to run an appliance?' sheet and Consumer Reports (updated Oct 2025).

items.head: Find the watts
items.body: Read the label on the controller or heater. If two controls, add them.

items.head: Find your rate
items.body: Your bill shows cents per kWh; add delivery charges. The US average is 18.16¢.

items.head: Multiply
items.body: Watts ÷ 1,000 × hours = kWh. 1,500 W × 8 h = 12 kWh.

items.head: Price it
items.body: kWh × your rate. 12 kWh × $0.18 = $2.16 a night.

items.head: Cut it down
items.body: A thermostat cycles a heater off; auto-off stops a pad after 10 hours.

items.head: Compare
items.body: Run the same sum for what you would use instead and keep the cheaper night.
